models.collectorNote: 1959 convertibles are the blue-chip fin cars, buy the best-restored example, because a full chrome-and-metal restoration costs more than the car. Late ETCs are the bargain entry to the nameplate.

generations.name: Eldorado Biarritz / Seville
generations.note: The fin year. Twin bullet tail lights, a 390 V8, and air suspension on the Biarritz convertible, the high-water mark of American chrome-age design, for better and worse.

generations.name: Eldorado Touring Coupe
generations.note: The last Eldorado: clean Bill Mitchell-era surfacing, the Northstar V8 from 1993, and a front-drive layout the market had already moved past. A 2002 Collector Series closed the nameplate.

models.intro: Fifty years of America's idea of luxury, from the hand-built 1953 convertible through the tallest tailfins ever fitted to a production car, to the final front-drive coupé of 2002.

generations.name: Escalade
generations.note: The second generation is the icon: hip-hop's official vehicle, a 6.0 V8, and the template for every luxury full-size SUV since.

generations.name: Escalade / Escalade-V
generations.note: Independent rear suspension finally, hands-free Super Cruise, and the V: a supercharged 6.2 with 682 hp in a three-row SUV. The electric Escalade IQ extends the nameplate, not the platform.

models.intro: A Yukon Denali in a tuxedo that became a cultural fixture, and Cadillac's profit engine. The current car added a 38-inch curved OLED and a 682 hp V-Series.

models.collectorNote: Manual wagons are the grail; manual sedans are the value. All LSA cars want a supercharger coupler check and a diff that has seen fresh fluid.

generations.name: CTS-V (LSA)
generations.note: A detuned ZR1 engine, magnetic dampers, and a 7:59 Nürburgring time that made it the fastest production sedan in the world at launch. Offered as sedan, coupé, and the immortal wagon.

generations.name: CTS-V (LT4)
generations.note: The LT4 from the Z06, 640 hp, 200 mph, and automatic only, which is why the gen-2 manual wagon keeps appreciating past it.

models.intro: Corvette engines in a Cadillac sedan, three generations running. The second-gen wagon with a manual gearbox is one of the most collectible American cars of the 2010s.

models.collectorNote: Manual cars are the future collectibles. Precision Package cars and early production numbers are the ones collectors are already circling.

generations.name: CT5-V Blackwing
generations.note: The hand-built LT4 makes 668 hp here. GM's engineers got the manual signed off as a deliberate statement, when it's gone, there will be nothing like it left.

models.intro: The last of its kind: a supercharged V8, rear-wheel drive, and a six-speed manual with no-lift shift, in a segment that went hybrid and all-wheel drive. Cadillac kept it in production because demand refused to die.
